gloss: misjudgment; bad call (in sports or law)

forms.label: Past polite
forms.negative: {誤審|ごしん}しませんでした

forms.label: ている past
forms.negative: {誤審|ごしん}していなかった

forms.label: ている past polite
forms.negative: {誤審|ごしん}していませんでした

definitions.explanation: An incorrect judgment or decision, especially by a referee in sports or a judge in legal proceedings. Most commonly used in the context of sports officiating.

examples.japanese: {審判|しんぱん}の{誤審|ごしん}で{試合|しあい}が{荒|あ}れた。
examples.english: The referee's bad call threw the game into chaos.

examples.japanese: あれは{明|あき}らかな{誤審|ごしん}だった。
examples.english: That was clearly a bad call.

examples.japanese: ビデオ{判定|はんてい}の{導入|どうにゅう}で{誤審|ごしん}が{大幅|おおはば}に{減|へ}った。
examples.english: The introduction of video review has greatly reduced bad calls.

notes: Composed of {誤|ご} (error, mistake) + {審|しん} (judge, examine). Primarily a sports term, used when referees or umpires make incorrect calls. Common collocations: {誤審|ごしん}をする (to make a bad call), {誤審|ごしん}{問題|もんだい} (officiating controversy), {誤審|ごしん}を{認|みと}める (to acknowledge a bad call). Related to the growing use of VAR (ビデオ・アシスタント・レフェリー) in soccer and video {判定|はんてい} (video review) in various sports. Part of the {誤〜|ご〜} prefix family: {誤解|ごかい} (misunderstanding), {誤用|ごよう} (misuse), {誤報|ごほう} (false report).
